name: Winner, Non-Winner & Loser Scripts
oneLine: Berne classifies scripts by outcome: winning (declared purpose met comfortably), losing or hamartic (purpose not met, in degrees up to death or disaster), or non-winning/banal (plays it safe, never a big win or a big loss).
whatYouDid: You helped Yusuf toward a winning move on a small scale - pacing himself to get both tonight's fun and tomorrow's clear head - instead of colluding with the After script's assumption that one has to cost the other.

fromBook.quote: A winner always has additional options, and that is how he wins... A non-winner sometimes wins and sometimes loses, but never very big in either direction, because he doesn't take risks.

expand.definition: 'Winning' is relative to your own declared purpose, not to money or status - Berne's own example of the happy, fulfilled hermit still counts as a winner. Losing scripts are graded first- to third-degree (hamartic) by how severe and socially visible the payoff is.
expand.otherFraming: Steiner's own vocabulary for the same territory is tragic/hamartic versus banal rather than loser versus non-winner - the same three-way split, with Steiner's three banal scripts (Lovelessness, Mindlessness, Joylessness) filling in what TA Today leaves more general.
expand.tryThisToday: Name one area of your life you'd currently call non-winning rather than losing or winning, and write one risk you've been avoiding there precisely because it's comfortable not to take it.
